panels.figure_caption: Computed Tomography (CT, coronal-oblique reconstruction) of the sternum in a 48-year-old male affected by osteopetrosis (ADO type 2). The so-called ‘bone in bone’ appearance is detectable with a well-defined increased density within the skeletal segment involved (arrows).
in_text_mentions: (3) The so-called ‘bone-within-a-bone’ or ‘bone-in-bone’ appearance, characterized by the presence of focal areas of sclerosis within a skeletal segment resembling another bone within the affected bone (Figure 3), which can be mostly found in phalanges, vertebrae, iliac wings, and long bones.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a lateral spinal radiograph from a 50-year-old male with ADO type 2 osteopetrosis and demonstrates the captioned sandwich-vertebrae sign. panels.figure_caption: Conventional radiography (lateral projection, (A)) and Computed Tomography (CT Sagittal reconstruction, (B)) of the spine of a 50-year-old male affected by osteopetrosis (ADO type 2). Well-defined areas of increased bone density are detectable on the vertebral endplates (arrowhead), configuring the so-called ‘sandwich vertebrae’ appearance.
in_text_mentions: (4) Well-defined sclerosis and the thickening of the vertebral endplate, the so-called “sandwich vertebrae” (Figure 4), and the ill-defined increased density of the vertebral endplates at multiple contiguous levels, the so-called “rugger-jersey” spine, which is, however, more typical of hyperparathyroidism [25,26]; this sign is more frequently encountered in ADO type 2 osteopetrosis.

Caption: “complete and marked sclerosis of the whole vertebrae in ARO type (B).”

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Patient radiograph of ADO type 2 osteopetrosis showing the characteristic rugger-jersey spine pattern of sclerotic vertebral endplates. [raw subtype: ADO type 2] B: Patient radiograph of autosomal recessive osteopetrosis showing marked diffuse sclerosis involving the entire vertebral bodies, contrasting with the endplate-predominant pattern in panel A. [raw subtype: ARO]
panels.attribution_text: Spinnato et al. Spectrum of Skeletal Imaging Features in Osteopetrosis: Inheritance Pattern and Radiological Associations.. Genes 2022. doi:10.3390/genes13111965. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 8.
panels.figure_caption: Different pattern of bone sclerosis in different type of osteopetrosis. Conventional radiographies (AP projection) in osteopetrosis ADO type 2 (A) and ARO (B) show different type of abnormally increased bone density: well-defined sclerosis of vertebral endplate (‘rugger jersey spine’—(A)) in ADO type 2, and complete and marked sclerosis of the whole vertebrae in ARO type (B).
in_text_mentions: It is well known that the different genetic patterns of osteopetrosis reflect in different clinical manifestations, prognosis, age of symptoms onset, and nonetheless different radiological features (Figure 8).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Patient radiograph showing the characteristic sandwich-vertebra appearance and diffuse osteosclerosis of osteopetrosis. [raw subtype: benign autosomal dominant osteopetrosis] B: Patient radiograph demonstrates diffuse skeletal osteosclerosis involving the pelvis and lower limbs, a characteristic manifestation of osteopetrosis. [raw subtype: benign autosomal dominant osteopetrosis] C: Skull radiograph shows homogeneous diffuse sclerosis characteristic of osteopetrosis. [raw subtype: benign autosomal dominant osteopetrosis] D: Patient CT demonstrates marked skull sclerosis with optic foraminal narrowing, directly captioned as a manifestation of osteopetrosis; associated ventricular dilatation is outside the supplied vocabulary. [raw subtype: benign autosomal dominant osteopetrosis]
panels.attribution_text: Rashid et al. A novel missense mutation in the CLCN7 gene linked to benign autosomal dominant osteopetrosis: a case series.. Journal of medical case reports 2013. doi:10.1186/1752-1947-7-7. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: X-rays and computed tomography scan image of the patient showing bone thickening. Radiograph shows typical (A) vertebral endplate thickening (sandwich vertebrae sign) of the rib and vertebrae, (B) diffuse thickening of pelvic and lower limb bones, and (C) homogenous sclerotic skull bones. (D) A computed tomography scan image of the patient’s brain showing an increased thickened bone density, homogenously sclerotic skull bones encroaching on both optic foramens, and mild dilatation of the lateral and third ventricle with normal fourth ventricle.
in_text_mentions: The index patient (Case 1) often complained of back pains. Skeletal radiography (Figure 1A-C) showed a diffuse increase in bone density with evidence of a sandwich appearance in the vertebrae and iliac wings (bone-in-bone). The computed tomography (CT) scan (Figure 1D) showed increased thickened bone density, homogenously sclerotic skull bones, encroaching on both optic foramens, and mild dilatation of lateral and third ventricle with normal fourth ventricle.
